haiku-low.q1: The 02:00 UTC scheduler starts it. It extracts orders with updated_at after W minus 2 h, up to the replica clock at snapshot start, including soft-deleted rows flagged is_deleted.
haiku-low.q2: updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit, and bulk transactions stay open up to 90 min. The row can appear on the replica up to 90 min after its updated_at.
haiku-low.q3: Every app write bumps updated_at. The next night extracts the changed row again, and the conditional MERGE replaces the older version in fact_orders.
haiku-low.q4: The app sets deleted_at (soft delete). The next night extracts it as is_deleted = true and the MERGE updates the row. Nothing is ever removed from fact_orders.
haiku-low.q5: Step 5 rolls back, so fact_orders and W stay unchanged. The run is marked failed, retried after 15 min, up to three attempts total. After the third failure, on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards keep showing the last committed fact_orders, the previous committed state. A staleness alert is posted to the #data-alerts channel.
haiku-low.q7: The Sunday reconciliation finds the mismatch on the order's creation day and reloads that whole day, re-extracting and merging all orders created that day.
haiku-low.q8: The conditional MERGE on order_id inserts unmatched rows, updates only when the staged updated_at is newer, and skips the rest, so each order_id keeps one row.
haiku-low.q9: Stored in etl_watermark as W. It is set to the upper bound (replica clock at snapshot start) in the same warehouse transaction as the MERGE, at commit, only on success.
haiku-low.q10: Step 5 is one warehouse transaction: the MERGE, W update and succeeded status commit together. Dashboards read only fact_orders, so they see all of a night's changes or none.
haiku-low.q11: The failed attempt's staged rows are discarded, since each attempt starts by truncating stg_orders. The retry reads the same W, extracts from W minus 2 h to a fresh upper bound.
haiku-low.q12: It re-extracts every order created on a mismatched day from the replica, applies them via the same conditional MERGE in its own transaction, and does not change the high-water mark W.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts it at 02:00 UTC. It extracts orders from the replica with updated_at after (W minus 2 h) up to upper (the replica clock at snapshot start), read in one snapshot. is_deleted = deleted_at is not null.
sonnet.q2: Bulk imports hold transactions open for up to 90 min, and updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit. So a row can appear on the replica up to 90 min after its updated_at.
sonnet.q3: Every app write bumps updated_at, so the next night's extract picks up the changed row again. The MERGE updates the fact_orders row because the staged updated_at is newer.
sonnet.q4: Deletes are soft: the app sets deleted_at, which is a write that bumps updated_at. The next night extracts it with is_deleted = true and the MERGE updates the row. The row stays in fact_orders and is never removed.
sonnet.q5: Nothing is committed to fact_orders or W. The etl_runs row is marked failed. If fewer than 3 attempts have been made tonight, it waits 15 min and retries. After the third failure it pages on-call.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards keep showing the last committed fact_orders. A staleness alert is posted to the #data-alerts channel, because no succeeded etl_runs row exists for tonight.
sonnet.q7: The next Sunday reconciliation. It compares the last 30 order-creation days, finds a mismatch on that order's creation day, and reloads every order created that day. (Alternatively, the order being written again.)
sonnet.q8: The MERGE on order_id is conditional. It inserts if there is no match, updates only if the staged updated_at is newer, and skips if not newer. So each order_id keeps exactly one row.
sonnet.q9: In the etl_watermark table in the warehouse, as a single row W. W is set to the attempt's upper bound (replica clock at snapshot start), in the same transaction as the MERGE, at Step 5 just before COMMIT.
sonnet.q10: Step 5 is a single warehouse transaction, so the MERGE, W update and run status commit together. Dashboards read only fact_orders, so they see all of a night's changes or none. They never read stg_orders.
sonnet.q11: The next attempt empties stg_orders (TRUNCATE at Step 1), so the staged data is discarded. It reads the same W, so the lower bound is again W minus 2 h. It takes a fresh upper bound and re-extracts.
sonnet.q12: It TRUNCATEs stg_orders and re-extracts every order created on a mismatched day. It applies them with the same conditional MERGE in its own transaction. It does not change W.
